en.name: Bulgur
en.summary: Bulgur is durum wheat that has been parboiled, dried and cracked, which is why it needs only soaking rather than long cooking. Sealed in a cool, dry cupboard it keeps 6–12 months. It is a dry pantry staple and needs neither the fridge nor the freezer to reach that.
en.pantry: Keep bulgur in an airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard, where it runs 6–12 months. The parboiling before drying is what makes it more stable than plain cracked wheat — some of the enzymes that would otherwise work on the germ oil have already been knocked out — but it is still a whole-wheat product with the bran on, so it will stale rather than keeping forever. Fine bulgur, being more finely cracked, has more surface exposed and goes flat sooner than coarse pilaf grades.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for bulgur, so none is given here, and in a normal kitchen it does not need one — a sealed jar in the cupboard covers the realistic life of a bag. If you live somewhere very hot and humid, an airtight jar in the fridge is a reasonable precaution against both damp and pantry insects, provided you bring it up to room temperature before opening it so moisture does not condense on the grain. Soaked or cooked bulgur is a different food and must be refrigerated.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for bulgur either. Freezing a sealed bag is a practical trick for a large bulk purchase — it stops any weevil eggs and slows the bran oil oxidising — but it is not a documented shelf life, and this page will not turn a habit into a number. For most households the cupboard figure is the one that matters.
spoilage: A bitter or paint-like smell from the oil in the bran and germ.
A musty, damp smell, or clumping in what should be free-running grain.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust at the bottom of the jar.
Soaked bulgur that tastes flat and cardboardy however it is dressed.
tips: Decant the bag into an airtight jar and date the lid.
Buy coarse bulgur for pilaf and fine for tabbouleh — and buy the size you will use.
Keep it away from the stove; heat costs more shelf life than time does.
Soaked bulgur goes in the fridge, covered, not back in the cupboard.

faq.a: 6–12 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard.

faq.q: Does bulgur need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. A sealed jar in a cool cupboard is enough; the fridge is only worth considering in a very hot, humid kitchen.
It usually stales rather than spoils — the bran oil turns and the flavour goes flat. Damp storage, mould or pantry insects are the real reasons to throw it out.

zh.name: 布格麥
zh.summary: 布格麥是杜蘭小麥先半煮熟、烘乾後再壓碎的產品，所以通常泡開就能吃，不必久煮。密封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃可放 6～12 個月。它是乾燥的常備食材，不需要冰箱或冷凍庫也能達到這個期限。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐，放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，可放 6～12 個月。烘乾前的半煮熟是它比一般碎小麥穩定的原因——會作用在胚芽油脂上的部分酵素已經先被破壞掉了——但它仍然是帶麩皮的全麥製品，所以會走味，不會永遠不變。細顆粒的布格麥因為碎得細、表面積大，比粗顆粒的抓飯用等級更早變得平淡。
zh.fridge: 布格麥沒有公布的冷藏期限，本頁也不給；在一般家庭裡它也不需要——密封罐放櫥櫃已經涵蓋一包的實際使用期。如果你住在非常濕熱的地方，密封罐放冰箱是防潮防蟲的合理措施，但開封前一定要先回到室溫，免得水氣凝在麥粒上。泡過或煮過的布格麥就是另一種食物了，必須冷藏。
zh.freezer: 布格麥也沒有給冷凍數字。把密封袋整包冷凍，對大量採購是個實用手法——可以中止蟲卵、延緩麩皮油脂氧化——但那不是有出處的保存期限，本頁不會把一個習慣寫成一個數字。對大多數家庭來說，櫥櫃那個數字才是重點。
spoilage: 聞到麩皮與胚芽油脂走油耗後的苦味或油漆味。
有潮霉味，或本該鬆散的麥粒結成塊。
罐底出現絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
泡開後不管怎麼調味都平淡如紙板。
tips: 整袋倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。
抓飯買粗顆粒、塔布勒沙拉買細顆粒——而且買你用得完的量。
遠離爐火；高溫奪走的壽命比時間還多。
泡開的布格麥要加蓋冷藏，不要放回櫥櫃。

faq.a: 密封罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，6～12 個月。
不需要。密封罐放陰涼櫥櫃就夠了；只有在非常濕熱的廚房才值得考慮冰箱。
多半是走味而不是腐敗——麩皮油脂變質、風味變平。受潮發霉或生蟲，才是真正該丟掉的理由。
